newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE'S CAREER BEST 61 PUTS PRESSURE ON TORRANCE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE'S CAREER BEST 61 PUTS PRESSURE ON TORRANCE.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie scored a spectacular career-best 10-under-par 61 in the European Masters on Saturday, losing his chance of a rare sub-60 round when the wind gusted over the closing holes.
The 33-year-old world number six began the day eight shots behind fellow Scot Sam Torrance, but his great round pulled him up to just one behind Torrance's 17-under-par 196 aggregate.
Torrance, who seemed in control after his second round 63, actually trailed his compatriot after Montgomerie scored his 10th birdie of the day at the 14th hole.
But Torrance, playing two holes behind, birdied the 13th and 14th and carded a 68 to regain the lead as Montgomerie could make no further inroads against par on the closing four holes.
Montgomerie's score was the lowest in Europe this season, though still a shot off the course record of 60 recorded by Briton Jamie Spence when he won in 1992.
"The only time I thought of 59 was when I birdied 14. I only had four pars to that point and the rest were all birdie chances," Montgomerie said.

"I thought then there was a distinct possibility. I only needed two more birdies and both 15 and 17 were on with another good chance at 18. But then the wind began to gust all over the place and that did me.
"I hit a great drive and four iron at the par-five 15th, but the wind dropped at the wrong time and my approach fell just short and I didn't get up and down.
"At 17 the wind took my birdie putt a few inches to the left at the wrong moment and at the 18th the wind again took my sand iron way to the right."
Montgomerie was, however, pleased with his best-ever round.

"I did not hit one bad shot and I've never previously scored lower than 63," he said. "I have shot two 65s in majors in America and maybe they were more important, but this is the best I've ever played.
"When I get back to my hotel, I won't be disappointed at missing 59 or elated at the way I played.
"I shall just be pleased that I shall annoy Sam Torrance. We are very good friends, but I have made his life far more difficult tomorrow."
Torrance agreed. He felt his best moment was at the last, where he came out of a bunker to four feet and holed out for a par four.
"That last putt kept me in the lead," said Torrance. "And it could be very important tomorrow. But Monty is like a rash, he never goes away."

Montgomerie and Torrance, first and second on last year's European Order of Merit, have further cause to be pleased. If they finish first and second on Sunday, Montgomerie will return to the top of the Order of Merit ahead of Ian Woosnam and Torrance will seal a place in the Volvo Masters at Valderrama next month.

It looks like a two-horse race for the first prize of 127,950 pounds sterling ($200,300) for Briton Paul Curry, in third place after a 65, is five shots off the pace and fourth-placed Lee Westwood is two shots further back.
